name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
Input and alignment — img.filtDFF.left/right were cropped to their shared imaging length; FicTrac variables were linearly interpolated to img.t without endpoint extrapolation.
Artifact rejection — points with dF/F > 10, local-median residual > 25 robust SD, or frame jump > 25 robust SD were masked with ±30 ms padding; source MAT files were unchanged.
Behavior — forward, lateral, signed yaw velocity, yaw speed, total speed, x/y position; positive yaw follows the local convention for rightward turns.
Bilateral states — each side was robustly z-scored; both-high required left and right z ≥ 1, both-low required z ≤ -1; states lasted ≥200 ms and gaps ≤100 ms were merged.
Coordination — centered 1 s rolling Pearson correlation; strongly coordinated epochs required r ≥ 0.6 and lasted ≥200 ms.
Event analysis — behavior was aligned to state entry from -3 to +3 s; pre/post forward comparisons used -1 to -0.2 s and +0.2 to +1 s.
Turn removal — each side was regressed on signed yaw velocity and yaw speed; residual dF/F was correlated with all kinematic variables.
Movement QC — percent moving was the fraction of FicTrac samples with total speed ≥ 3.

text:
Right-minus-left activity correlates with signed yaw in 21/21 trials (mean r = -0.266)
Left and right copies show opposite-signed yaw relationships
Cross-correlations peak near zero lag in representative trials
Bilateral-high epochs also show greater yaw speed than bilateral-low epochs
Forward-speed effects remain mixed across trials and events
Interpretation: a strong directional component plus weaker common-mode modulation
